propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of RAD decision dismissing his appeal of RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The applicant, Ebel Feliznor, is seeking the judicial review of the Refugee Appeal Division [RAD] decision of February 6, 2019, dismissing his appeal of the Refugee Protection Division [RPD] decision.

propositions.text: RPD and RAD concluded applicant excluded from refugee definition under section 98 IRPA and Article 1E Convention.
propositions.quote: The RPD and the RAD concluded that the applicant was excluded from the definition of refugee and person in need of protection pursuant to section 98 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA], and Article 1E of the United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, July 28, 1951, 189 UNTS 137 [Convention].

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of RAD decision dismissing his appeal; RPD and RAD found applicant excluded from refugee definition under IRPA and Convention.

propositions.text: Applicant is Haitian citizen who fled due to fear after armed individuals tried to take his land and harvests.
propositions.quote: The applicant is a citizen of Haiti. He fled Haiti, alleging he feared returning since armed individuals attempted to take his agricultural land and his harvests.

propositions.text: Applicant left Haiti for Brazil in 2011, lived there 5.5 years, obtained permanent resident status.
propositions.quote: In February 2011, the applicant left Haiti for Brazil, where he lived for five and a half years. He obtained permanent resident status in Brazil.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is Haitian who fled due to threats, lived in Brazil for 5.5 years and obtained permanent resident status there.

propositions.text: In 2016, applicant received death threat in Brazil, hid, then left for US in 2017, then to Canada claiming refugee status.
propositions.quote: In August 2016, the applicant received a death threat from the spouse of a woman he had kissed... he hid at his friends’ place before leaving Brazil for the United States, where he arrived on January 5, 2017. On August 17, 2017, the applicant left the United States for Canada, and he claimed refugee status that same day.

propositions.text: Applicant fears Brazil due to threats and persecution against Haitians and black people.
propositions.quote: The applicant alleged a fear with regard to Brazil because of the threats by the spouse and persecution against Haitians and black people.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant received death threat in Brazil, fled to US then Canada claiming refugee status, fearing persecution in Brazil.

propositions.text: RPD dismissed claim because permanent resident status in Brazil gave rights like nationals; no serious persecution risk shown.
propositions.quote: The RPD dismissed the applicant’s claim for refugee protection on the ground that he had permanent resident status in Brazil. This status gave him essentially the same rights as Brazilian nationals, and the applicant did not show a serious possibility of persecution or risk to life, or risk of cruel and unusual punishment pursuant to sections 97 and 98 of the IRPA should he return to Brazil.

paragraphs.summary: RPD dismissed claim as applicant's permanent resident status in Brazil gave him rights like nationals and no serious persecution risk shown.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed RPD decision on appeal.
propositions.quote: The applicant appealed this decision but the RAD confirmed it.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant appealed but RAD confirmed RPD decision.

propositions.text: Issue is whether RAD decision is reasonable, including applicant's arguments on status, evidence, and persecution criteria.
propositions.quote: The only issue is whether the RAD decision is reasonable. This issue includes the applicant’s arguments that the RAD misunderstood his status in Brazil, granted too much importance to certain evidence it determined undermined his credibility and improperly applied the persecution criteria set out in the Convention.

paragraphs.summary: Issue is whether RAD decision is reasonable, including applicant's arguments on status, evidence, and persecution criteria.

propositions.text: Standard of review for exclusion under Article 1E and section 98 IRPA is reasonableness.
propositions.quote: The applicable standard of review for determining whether the facts lead to an exclusion pursuant to Article 1E of the Convention and section 98 of the IRPA is reasonableness (Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Zeng, 2010 FCA 118 at para 11 [Zeng]; Noel v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2018 FC 1062 at paras 14–15).

paragraphs.summary: Standard of review for exclusion under Article 1E and section 98 IRPA is reasonableness.

propositions.text: Vavilov decision does not change reasonableness standard here; no need for submissions on standard of review.
propositions.quote: The recent Supreme Court decision in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov], does not change this conclusion... it is not necessary to request submissions from the parties on the standard of review or its application.

propositions.text: Vavilov and Canada Post Corp confirm no unfairness arises applying reasonableness standard here.
propositions.quote: As in the Supreme Court decision in Canada Post Corp v Canadian Union of Postal Workers, 2019 SCC 67 at para 24 [Canada Post Corp], in this case, with the application of the Vavilov analysis “[n]o unfairness arises from this as the applicable standard of review and the result would have been the same under the Dunsmuir framework”.

paragraphs.summary: Vavilov does not change reasonableness standard; no unfairness applying it here per Vavilov and Canada Post Corp.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires internally coherent, justified analysis; challenger must show flaws central enough to render decision unreasonable.
propositions.quote: To be reasonable, a decision must be based on an internally coherent analysis that is justified in light of the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on it... The party challenging the decision must satisfy the Court that “any shortcomings or flaws . . . are sufficiently central or significant to render the decision unreasonable”

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires coherent, justified analysis; challenger must show flaws central enough to make decision unreasonable.

propositions.text: RAD erred by not considering conditional nature of applicant's permanent resident status in Brazil.
propositions.quote: The applicant submits that the RAD erred in its analysis of the exclusion factors pursuant to Article 1E of the Convention and section 98 of the IRPA by not considering the conditional nature of his status.

propositions.text: Applicant argues permanent resident status valid for eight-year intervals and lost after two-year absence under Brazilian law.
propositions.quote: He does not deny that he obtained permanent residence in Brazil but states that it was valid for intervals of eight years, and that Brazilian law indicates that a permanent resident loses their status after a two-year absence from the country.

propositions.text: Applicant argued before RPD and RAD that residence was conditional and RAD ignored evidence of conditions and obligations.
propositions.quote: This is why the applicant argued before the RPD and the RAD that his residence was conditional. The RAD did not consider the evidence indicating that a permanent resident must reside in Brazil and carry out the activities prescribed by the terms of his status, and that a permanent resident must have good reasons to leave Brazil.

propositions.text: National Documentation Package confirms permanent resident status is conditional.
propositions.quote: The objective evidence in the National Documentation Package confirms that permanent resident status is conditional.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD erred by ignoring conditional nature of his permanent resident status and related evidence.

propositions.text: Applicant cites Zeng that panel must weigh factors to find exclusion; RAD failed to weigh these factors here.
propositions.quote: The applicant adds that Zeng states that the panel that determines whether Article 1E of the Convention should apply in a specific case must weigh various factors to make a finding of exclusion. In the present case, the RAD did not weigh these factors.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD failed to weigh factors for exclusion as required by Zeng.

propositions.text: Applicant had good reasons to leave Brazil due to discrimination and persecution of Haitians and black people.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the applicant states that he had good reasons to leave Brazil. He does not have the same rights as Brazilians because of the systematic violations of the human rights of Haitians and black people in Brazil.

propositions.text: Applicant testified Haitians are pursued and killed in Brazil; objective evidence confirms fear including Special Rapporteur's report.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, he stated that Haitians are pursued and killed in Brazil. The objective evidence confirms this fear, in particular the Report of the Special Rapporteur on minority issues on her mission to Brazil (February 9, 2016, National Documentation Package on Brazil), which indicates that, after a migration of a considerable number of Haitians to Brazil, the Haitians were victims of violent attacks carried out for reasons related to race and nationality.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues he had good reasons to leave Brazil due to persecution and discrimination against Haitians and blacks, supported by evidence.

propositions.text: RAD imposed excessive burden by requiring serious possibility of persecution; Brazilian state ineffective protecting Afro-Brazilians and Haitians.
propositions.quote: The RAD agreed that the evidence shows that Brazil is a country where the rate of violence is very high and where there are incidents of discrimination and racism. However, by requiring the applicant to show this was the equivalent of a serious possibility of persecution, the RAD imposed an excessive burden of proof. The objective evidence already shows that the Brazilian state is ineffective at protecting its own Afro-Brazilian citizens. It is inconceivable that the Brazilian state would be more effective with regard to Haitians.

propositions.text: RAD neglected applicant's statements about death threat and discrimination in forms.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the RAD neglected to note that the applicant states in his forms that he was threatened with death by the husband of the woman he had kissed and that he faced discrimination and racism in Brazil.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD imposed excessive burden and neglected his statements about death threat and discrimination.

propositions.text: RAD overemphasized minor discrepancies undermining credibility, ignored explanations and death threat evidence.
propositions.quote: On the issue of credibility, the applicant submits that the RAD placed too much emphasis on the minor issues in his evidence, ignoring the fact that he was threatened with death. The RAD affirmed the RPD conclusion that the discrepancies between the applicant’s account in his forms and the account in his testimony undermine his credibility. The RAD did not consider his explanations for the minor differences.

propositions.text: RAD gave too much importance to applicant not applying for refugee protection in the US.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the RAD granted too much importance to the fact the applicant did not apply for refugee protection when he was in the United States.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD overemphasized minor credibility issues and gave too much weight to not applying for refugee protection in US.

propositions.text: Applicant submits RAD decision is unreasonable due to errors and evidence of persecution and death threat.
propositions.quote: In light of the accumulation of errors committed by the RAD and considering the applicant’s evidence that he fled Brazil after a death threat and because he was persecuted because of his race and origin, the applicant submits that the RAD decision is unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits RAD decision is unreasonable due to errors and evidence of persecution and death threat.

propositions.text: Court not convinced; RAD did not err in assessing evidence or law; decision reasonable under Vavilov standard.
propositions.quote: I am not convinced. The applicant obtained permanent resident status in Brazil, and the RAD did not err in its assessment of the evidence or the application of the law on this issue. The RAD conclusions are “based on an internally coherent chain of reasoning and [are] justified in light of the relevant legal and factual constraints” as required under the reasonableness standard of review stated in Vavilov (Canada Post Corp, at para 2).

paragraphs.summary: Court not convinced; RAD's assessment and decision are reasonable under Vavilov standard.

propositions.text: Applicant does not deny permanent resident status at hearing; RAD correctly dismissed argument that status was conditional and rights unequal due to discrimination.
propositions.quote: The applicant does not deny that at the time of the hearing before the RPD he had permanent resident status in Brazil. He submits that this status was conditional and that he did not have the same rights as Brazilian nationals because there was discrimination and racism against Haitian nationals. The RAD correctly dismissed these arguments.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant admits permanent resident status; RAD correctly dismissed conditional status and rights inequality arguments.

propositions.text: Exclusion under Article 1E and section 98 IRPA assessed at RPD hearing date; RAD applied this standard correctly.
propositions.quote: The exclusion set out in Article 1E of the Convention and section 98 of the IRPA must be assessed on the date of the hearing before the RPD (Majebi v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FCA 274 at para 7; Zeng at para 28). The RAD applied this standard in the present case.

propositions.text: RAD assessed applicant's conditional status and discrimination arguments and dismissed them based on facts and law.
propositions.quote: The RAD assessed the applicant’s argument that his status was conditional and did not grant him the same rights as Brazilian citizens because of the conditions in which Haitians currently live in Brazil. The RAD did not err in dismissing the applicant’s argument; its analysis was well founded on facts and law: The fact that a permanent resident has to fulfill obligations, such as live in the country and not commit crimes, does not mean that their status is not permanent. His status was still granted to him for an indeterminate period. The appellant does not need to re-qualify to be able to renew the permanent resident status, and his card will be re-issued automatically.

paragraphs.summary: Exclusion assessed at RPD hearing date; RAD correctly dismissed conditional status and discrimination arguments based on facts and law.

propositions.text: RAD found RPD did not err on credibility; noted significant discrepancies between forms and testimony undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The RAD also concluded that the RPD did not err in the assessment of the applicant’s credibility, and this conclusion is well founded in the evidence. The RAD noted significant discrepancies between the applicant’s account in his forms and the one he presented during his testimony. For example, in his forms, he alleged that Haitians are pursued and killed in Brazil, but he did not express this fear in his testimony. He stated that he experienced racism and discrimination at work but did not mention this in his forms.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found RPD did not err on credibility; noted discrepancies between forms and testimony undermining credibility.

propositions.text: RAD noted inconsistencies about woman kissed and death threat, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: As for the death threat, the RAD noted that the applicant described the woman he had kissed as a neighbour in his forms, whereas in his testimony it was a friend of a co-worker. The RAD concluded that there are significant inconsistencies between the facts related in the forms and those in the applicant’s testimony, which undermine his credibility.

propositions.text: Applicant says RAD overemphasized minor issues and neglected death threat evidence.
propositions.quote: The applicant states that the RAD put too much emphasis on minor issues and neglected to consider the fact he had received a death threat.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds inconsistencies undermining credibility; applicant argues RAD overemphasized minor issues and ignored death threat evidence.

propositions.text: Applicant's refugee claim is based on non-application of Article 1E and section 98, and a death threat from interaction with a woman
propositions.quote: The applicant’s refugee protection claim is based on two main points: the non-application of Article 1E of the Convention and section 98 of the IRPA, and the death threat due to his interaction with the woman.

propositions.text: Applicant's inconsistent description of the death threat is a significant issue
propositions.quote: The fact he described this in an inconsistent manner is not a minor issue.

propositions.text: Credibility evidence interpretation warrants considerable deference by reviewing court
propositions.quote: it must be noted that the interpretation of evidence on credibility warrants considerable deference by a reviewing court (Rahal v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2012 FC 319).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues refugee claim based on Article 1E and death threat; court finds inconsistency significant and cites Rahal for deference on credibility.

propositions.text: RAD found applicant did not rebut presumption that Brazilian state can protect citizens
propositions.quote: the RAD reviewed the evidence and concluded that the applicant had not rebutted the presumption that the Brazilian state was able to protect its citizens and residents.

propositions.text: RAD was not required but reasonably analyzed refugee status under Article 1E and section 98 given conclusion
propositions.quote: Even though the RAD was not required to address this issue, considering the conclusion that the applicant did not have refugee status pursuant to Article 1E of the Convention and section 98 of the IRPA... it was not unreasonable in this case to have conducted the analysis.

propositions.text: Reference to Celestin v Canada supports RAD's approach
propositions.quote: see discussion in Celestin v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2020 FC 97

paragraphs.summary: RAD found applicant failed to rebut Brazilian state protection presumption; RAD reasonably analyzed refugee status under Article 1E and section 98, citing Celestin.

propositions.text: RAD found Brazil has high violence, discrimination, racism
propositions.quote: The RAD concluded that the evidence shows that Brazil is a country with a very high rate of violence, where there are regular incidents of discrimination and racism.

propositions.text: RAD noted contradictions in applicant's testimony about problems in Brazil
propositions.quote: The RAD also noted the contradictions in the applicant’s testimony about the problems he had in Brazil.

propositions.text: Legal system ineffective against organized crime but this did not affect applicant
propositions.quote: The evidence indicates that the legal system is ineffective against organized criminality and drug traffickers, but this problem did not affect the applicant.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows discrimination against Afro-Brazilians aged 15-29; applicant is 40-year-old Haitian, so does not fit profile
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that the objective evidence deals with discrimination against Afro-Brazilians and, in particular, people from 15 to 29 years of age. Considering the applicant is a 40-year-old Haitian, the RAD concluded that he does not fit the profile in this report.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Brazil violent with discrimination; noted contradictions in applicant's testimony; legal issues did not affect applicant; applicant does not fit discrimination profile.

propositions.text: Court agrees RAD decision is reasonable
propositions.quote: To conclude, I agree that the RAD decision is reasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant did not show flaw central or significant enough to render decision unreasonable (citing Vavilov and Canada Post)
propositions.quote: The applicant did not show any “flaw . . . sufficiently central or significant to render the decision unreasonable” (Vavilov at para 100; Canada Post Corp at para 33).

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees RAD decision reasonable; applicant failed to show significant flaw per Vavilov and Canada Post precedents.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is dismissed.

propositions.text: No question of general importance for certification
propositions.quote: There is no question of general importance for certification.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review application and finds no question of general importance for certification.
